conservation.condition_narrative:
Paper label in the painting’s file from the painting’s original backing board: “Sprayed with a solution of n-butyl isobutyl methacrylate copolymer resin as a final protective surface coating,” then in pen: “April 29, 1955.” 
Minor inpainting and consolidation were undertaken in preparation for exhibition and loan.
conservation.report_notes: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by Baltimore Museum of Art in 2025.
conservation.technical_description:
The medium-weight, plain weave canvas is stretched onto a 4-member stretcher with “17” and “32” written on the stretcher verso. The canvas has been primed with a white priming layer which extends to the ends of the canvas. The canvas weave is strongly apparent through the thin paint and ground layers. Many skips in the paint reveal the ground below. 
The painting has an even, satin surface appearance. A label from the painting’s original backing board indicates that it was varnished with a synthetic resin in 1955. The varnish listed on the label is similar to that used by Caroline and Sheldon Keck to varnish many of O’Keeffe’s paintings, but the label does not directly attribute this work to them. 
The painting is framed in an artist’s original frame which was noted by Dr. Barbara Buhler Lynes to have been designed by Peter Bayle. The narrow metal frame is screwed into the sides of the canvas and has been painted to match the composition: it is primarily gray, but the sections of the frame where the painted waterfall touches it have been painted white (center of top and bottom frame members).
